scope: Independent read-only comparison of local-coding manuscript statements, exact model/quantifier contracts and proof outlines against actual Lean source endpoints and dependency architecture. No Lean/Lake/PDF execution or manuscript/proof edits by reviewer.

details: LocalQuery support is an arbitrary finite set of original rows; query functions may be nonlinear. Both query and halt are public-history functions after a finite helper is fixed.

GraphSeparatorBound distribution endpoint quantifies over every nonnegative normalized law on F, permits zero mass, and still requires all-F execution and correctness. D_w and H(Z) in bits match division by log 2.
Finite-family truncation preserves charged runs and their supports while allowing divergence off F.
The separator is an arbitrary function of helper and completed transcript; each used support forms a clique. Loss is d*b*|S| + b*sum component_size^2.
Worst-case form counts attained helper values, but requires finite ambient helper type exactly as prose states.
Virtual fiber fixes the protocol branch/helper parameter, transcript and separator values but does not condition on actual helper or correctness.
Full virtual fiber factorization is derived from query locality and component gluing; no product law is imposed on the correct subfamily.
The two conditional comparison budgets (volume and prefix code) are proved separately. Displayed entropy inequalities algebraically yield 2H(X) <= P+2H(Z)+E(q+r).
The full-fiber cardinal bound 2 log|A| <= log|R| + internal_free_bits is the SeparatorCount/SeparatorLeaf endpoint, with separator rows conditioned.
Both witnesses use d=2, b>0, empty separator and zero transcript. Symmetry family has deficit b and no helper entropy; full cube has helper XOR of off-diagonal entries and exactly b helper entropy.
The separate universal coefficient claims are supported by their explicit example endpoints; no simultaneous optimality of all constants is asserted.
Natural-valued ordinary finite treewidth, empty-graph convention, exact (L+1)|S| bound and separator-loss formula match Treewidth.
Arbitrary-law average treewidth endpoint is d*a^2/4+a/2-1, with a=max(epsilon-2(D_w+H(Z))/P,0), d,b>0.
The integer-threshold proof retains the positive a/2 correction; displayed identity and division by d are valid.
The asymptotic small-separator consequence now explicitly retains negligible deficit/helper entropy.
Arbitrary fixed row bijections and decoding maps, all-input correctness, original-row side information, fixed singleton/pair packets, and no helper exactly match RecodedXorCode.
Same-row pairs, self-XORs, repetitions and disconnected graphs are allowed; near pairs are defined by existence of a walk shorter than ell, so ell=0 and disconnected cases are correct.

Unanchored component flips preserve broadcast and raw bits outside their represented-row square at every basepoint. Disjoint free flip orbits justify the small-component count despite nonlinear recoding.
Integral bound, degree constant 6, and strengthened path/cycle error b*d*(sqrt(8(d+3))-4) match current endpoints. The integer square-root optimization algebra in the proof outline is valid.

Injective homomorphism into a nonempty cycle and path/subcycle specializations match the exact formal scope. The prose explicitly separates this packet format from arbitrary two-row linear functionals and from the first paper XOR-frame model.
Triangular updates depend on earlier incoming rows, bijectively in the own-row argument; causal second-stage updates use own and earlier incoming rows and need not be injective.
Three row permutations, arbitrary input/output local maps, bijective middle maps, triangular first stage, and causal second stage appear in the exact TwoStageRows.apply order.
Suffix I is defined using second.order after inverse middlePerm; input R and output J are the exact derived source/output support sets.
The record w_(I complement) and x_(R times J) is injective using BlockInjective of the middle inverse, raw correctness, and injectivity of transpose. Its cardinal exponent (d-r)*d*b+r^2*b is exact.
No extra bank, global intermediate map, private controller, or runtime-free primitive claim beyond the explicitly granted finite model is added.
TwoStageHelper ambient helper type is unrestricted, with only its finite image on F used for counts/entropy.
Exact counts include empty F; the real density assumption implies nonempty F and has no integer deficit rounding.
Every nonnegative normalized law on F, including zero masses, has D_w+H(Z)>=b*r*(d-r) and the quarter toll. Correctness remains required throughout F.
Finite-fiber entropy inequality is valid also for unnormalized nonnegative weights, and normalization supplies the stated Shannon entropy endpoint.
Asymptotic quarter-rate summary now explicitly assumes d tends to infinity and D_w=o(P).
Opening and closing scope statements explicitly distinguish finite coding architectures from arbitrary tape computations.
No normalization of arbitrary coded workspace to original-row access is assumed.
First-paper comparisons are framed as restricted-architecture progress, not a stronger native pass lower bound or proof of TCC/hint removal.
